newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA falls again on overseas fund selling.
newsitem.headline: SIA falls again on overseas fund selling.

text.p: Shares in Singapore Airlines Ltd fell further on Tuesday morning as brokers executed sell-orders put in place overnight by overseas investors.
SIA's foreign shares, followed most closely by fund managers, dropped to a low of Singapore $12.60, down 40 cents or three percent in early trade.
"News of the company's first-half results had not been fully taken in by European and U.S. clients by the time the market closed here yesterday," said one institutional dealer.

SIA's foreign share tranche dropped S$1.00 to S$13.00 on Monday after the national carrier reported a below consensus 7.2 percent rise in its net profit to S$560.5 million for the six months to September 30.
Local brokerage DBS Securities cut its recommendation on SIA's foreign shares to reduce from accumulate and its recommendation on the local shares to accumulate from buy.
SIA's local share fell five cents to S$7.50 on Tuesday.
The Business Times newspaper reported on Tuesday an unidentified local broker as saying SIA's foreign shares could drop to S$12.00 before attracting renewed overseas buying.
